questions.text: Shift reduce parsing belongs to a class of
questions.solution: Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

Without moving code, after e = c + a the values a, c, d, e are all live (c is still needed for x = c * c, and d, e for the else part). That is 4 live values at once.

After that, x replaces c, keeping at most 4 live. So 4 registers suffice and fewer will not.

Answer: 4

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

a stays live till the end (used in x [latex]\gt[/latex] a and y = a * a), and c is needed for d, e and x. While computing d or e, three values (a, c, the new result) are live, but there are only 2 registers.

So at least one spill is needed. Using code motion (computing things where they are needed) one spill is enough.

Answer: 1

questions.text:
Consider the following two sets of LR(1) items of an LR(1) grammar.

[latex]\begin{array}{l|l} X \rightarrow c.X, c∕d &X → c.X, \$\\ X \rightarrow .cX, c∕  d& X → .cX, \$\\ X \rightarrow .d, c∕ d & X → .d, \$ \end{array}[/latex]

Which of the following statements related to merging of the two sets in the corresponding LALR parser is/are FALSE?
1. Cannot be merged since look aheads are different.
2. Can be merged but will result in S-R conflict.
3. Can be merged but will result in R-R conflict.
4. Cannot be merged since goto on c will lead to two different sets.
questions.solution:
Both sets have the same core (same items, different lookaheads), so LALR merges them. The merged set has no reduce items (only shifts on c and d), so there is no S-R or R-R conflict. GOTO on c from both lead to sets that are also merged.

So all four statements are false.

Answer: 1, 2, 3 and 4
